messages:
maria: Quick design review—the rule stack visual weight feels off when a rule is disabled. Opacity + strike-through makes it hard to tell priority at a glance. Screenshot attached in thread :eyes:. Thoughts?

sam: I noticed that too. Suggest lowering disabled opacity to ~0.36 and adding a small 'disabled' pill left of the label so the number/priority stays visually anchored. Also check contrast on the struck text for a11y.

jordan: Agree with anchoring the number. Another idea: keep the priority number fixed in a left column (sticky) so reorders don’t make it jump around. Hover tooltip could show "effective priority after filters" when policies are filtered. Small copy tweak: replace "Invalid order" with "Rule conflict — review dependencies" so it's actionable.

alex: For the preview simulation, can we animate reordering to show destination? A subtle slide helps users understand where a rule will land. e.g.:
```css
.rule-item { transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); }
```
Also, when fallback rules are auto-inserted, show a toast explaining why.

kate: Keyboard + screen reader note: when reordering via keyboard, we need an aria-live region announcing new position ("Rule X moved to position 2"). Also set aria-grabbed on the dragged item. Make sure color isn't the only affordance for disabled state.

maria: Great. I'll update the Figma frames — will capture two a11y test cases (contrast & live announcements). Sam, can you run the contrast checks on the screenshot assets? Jordan, can you prototype the tooltip copy and show the filter interaction?

sam: Yep, I'll run axe/contrast and post results here later today. +1 on pill and sticky number :thumbsup:

jordan: On it — will mock tooltip text and the sticky-number layout in the next iteration.

deploy-bot: UI preview deployed to staging: https://staging.redwood.com/routing/editor (canary).

maria: Thanks — once staging is up, let's do a quick 10m walkthrough tomorrow morning and capture any microcopy changes. "Invalid order" -> "Rule conflict — check prerequisites" is my preferred change for the validation message.
